Definition: to be bitter or (causatively) to embitter, i.e. be painful
BiblicalUsage: The word means to be bitter or painful, and the law uses it for a plague that eats away at cloth or a house, a fretting leprosy that spreads and cannot be cleansed. Ezekiel uses it for the pricking brier and the grieving thorn that shall trouble Israel no more when God restores her.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the fretting plague is a picture of sin: it spreads quietly and eats what it touches, and only the priest's cleansing can name it clean. I hold that God's promise to remove the grieving thorn is the promise of the gospel, that what has eaten at us will not eat at us forever.
